title_en: How Do We Strengthen Our Faith?
body_ar: إن هذا من مهمات الإنسان و مما ينبغي أن يسأل عنه دائما فلإيمان هو أعز شيء يتحلى به الإنسان و هو محتاج لتقويته في كل الأوقات لأن الإيمان يزيد و ينقص و يجد و يصدأ و إنما يتقوى إيمان الإنسان بزيادة العمل الصالح المقرب من الله سبحانه و تعالى و زيادة الموعظة و الذكرى و زيادة العلم أيضا فهذا الذي يقوي إيمان الإنسان فالإنسان إذا أراد أن يقوي إيمانه لا بد أن يزيد من طاعاته لا يمكن أن يكون الإنسان الذي لا يتنفل و لا يذكر الله إلا قليلا في مستواه الإيماني كذلك الذي يحافظ على النوافل و يكثر ذكر الله و يختم القرآن و يتصدق و يصوم هذا لا يمكن أن يكون مساويا للأول فلهذا لا بد إذا أراد الإنسان تقوية إيمانه أن يزداد من الطاعات و بزيادة الطاعات يقوى الإيمان و يرسخ في النفوس.
body_en: This is among a person's most important concerns, and among the things he ought always to be asking about. Faith (īmān) is the most precious thing with which a person is adorned, and he stands in need of strengthening it at all times, because faith increases and decreases, and is made new and rusts. A person's faith is strengthened only by increasing the righteous deeds that bring him near to God, glorified and exalted, and by increasing admonition and reminder, and by increasing knowledge as well. This is what strengthens a person's faith. So if a person wants to strengthen his faith, he must increase his acts of obedience. It is not possible that a person who performs no voluntary prayers and remembers God only a little should be, in his level of faith, like one who keeps up the voluntary acts (nawāfil), and remembers God abundantly, and completes the Qur'an, and gives charity, and fasts — this one cannot be the equal of the first. So for this reason, if a person wants to strengthen his faith, he must increase in acts of obedience; and by increasing acts of obedience faith is strengthened and takes firm root in souls.

options: is made new and rusts (reading yajidd, from jadda)
is found and rusts (reading yajid, from wajada)
flags.note: CONFIRMS A READING FLAGGED ELSEWHERE. The same unvowelled يجد appears in record 571 of this slice, where the reading was flagged as uncertain. Here it is paired with yaṣdaʾ, 'rusts', which settles it: the pair is 'is made new / rusts', and the reading yajidd is correct. Recorded in both records so that a reviewer fixes the same reading in both.

flags.note: NOT A DUPLICATE, BUT WORTH RECORDING. Three records in this slice answer substantially the same question about strengthening or increasing faith: 554 ('How do we strengthen our faith?'), 570 ('What is the best way to develop faith?') and 571 ('What are the means of increasing faith?', an excerpt). The Arabic texts are entirely different from one another, so this is not the CMS duplication pattern seen at 561/563; it is three separate answers to one recurring question. Flagged so that the site does not present them as three unrelated items, and so that a reviewer can consider cross-linking them.

translator_notes: The date carried here is the CMS record date. Across this whole slice the site serves a bulk-upload timestamp of 19-27 December 2010, which is when the written archive was loaded into the site, not when the Sheikh gave the answer. date_is_cms_upload is set true. The real date of composition is not recoverable from the page and has not been guessed.
The Sheikh gives no scriptural evidence and no citation anywhere in this record, and none has been supplied.
'Acts of obedience' renders ṭāʿāt throughout; 'voluntary acts' renders nawāfil, per the glossary entry for nāfilah.
